findings.reason: forking the geometry-moment owner leaves four independent polygon-moment implementations inside `nova/equilibrium` that must stay numerically identical, and every future fix (orientation, padding, capacity) then has to be applied four times.
findings.text: `_straight_edge_monomial_moments` re-derives exact polygon monomial moments through the homogeneous recurrence, a mechanism the codebase already owns as `nova/equilibrium/separatrix_clip.py:_traced_polygon_moments` (line 850, the traced/jnp form) and `separatrix_clip._area_moments` (line 125, the host/numpy form); the plan's own reuse map (plan.html line 189) names `separatrix_clip._traced_polygon_moments` as the mechanism to "Generalise for the density moments", yet the landed design added two parallel reductions instead of generalising it

findings.reason: the plan's headline deliverable module is orphaned from the solve, so the design should either make it the production reduction or consolidate it into the existing owner, since a module that duplicates production algebra without being on the production path adds surface, not depth.
findings.text: the module hides the Green's-theorem edge tables and the orientation/padding logic behind `polygon_monomial_moments` and `polygon_density_moments`, but production never calls it: no module under `nova/` imports `polygon_moments` (only `tests/test_polygon_moments.py`, `benchmarks/exact_clip_closed_form_floor.py` and `benchmarks/xpoint_cell_wedge_oracle.py`), while the production clip route runs `clip_quadrature._sampled_arc_polynomial_moments` over `_straight_edge_monomial_moments`

findings.reason: the correct prior art is the geometric-moment owner in `separatrix_clip`, so the survey's mis-citation is part of why the design forked a new reduction instead of extending the existing one.
findings.text: the plan's §2 asserts the polygon-analytic machinery "already used for the kernel blocks (nova/biot/polygonanalytic.py, polygon_analytic_flux_moments) integrates the geometric moments of the region exactly"; opening that function shows it computes the exact fixed-section flux blocks (G_0, G_R, G_Z), the area means of `(R-R_c)K_psi` and `(Z-Z_c)K_psi`, i.e. kernel-weighted integrals, not the density/geometric monomial moments the plan needs, so the reuse survey mis-identified the reusable mechanism

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the polygon-moment reduction is spread across three equilibrium modules (`polygon_moments.py`, `clip_quadrature.py`, `separatrix_clip.py`) rather than hidden behind one interface, so the same algebra is carried twice in production and once more as an oracle.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — `nova/equilibrium/clip_quadrature.py:_straight_edge_monomial_moments` and `nova/equilibrium/polygon_moments.py` both re-implement polygon geometric moments already owned by `nova/equilibrium/separatrix_clip.py:_traced_polygon_moments`.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan's §2 cites `polygon_analytic_flux_moments` (nova/biot/polygonanalytic.py:1787) as the mechanism that integrates "the geometric moments of the region exactly", but that function returns kernel-weighted flux blocks (G_0, G_R, G_Z), not geometric monomial moments.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — `polygon_density_moments` adds the quadratic-to-monomial contraction on top of the monomial table; it is a real reduction, not a forwarding layer over existing machinery.
